card.title: Cross product — area, torque and the right-hand rule

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The vector product $\vec{C} = \vec{A} \times \vec{B}$ of two vectors is a third vector: magnitude $AB\sin\theta$, direction perpendicular to the plane of $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ by the right-hand rule (fingers along A, curl toward B, thumb gives C). Dot product measures sameness (projection); cross product measures perpendicularity (area).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: |A × B| = AB sinθ,  0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°  ·  A × B = AB sinθ n̂  ·  cyclic: î×ĵ=k̂, ĵ×k̂=î, k̂×î=ĵ  ·  î×î = ĵ×ĵ = k̂×k̂ = 0

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Defined for exactly two vectors in 3D space only (no A×B×C without brackets). θ is the smaller angle between them, 0° to 180°, so sinθ ≥ 0 and the magnitude is never negative.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Parallel (θ = 0°/180°) → A×B = 0, the test for parallelism. Perpendicular (θ = 90°) → |A×B| = AB, the maximum. Anti-commutative: B×A = −(A×B). Distributive over addition: A×(B+C) = A×B + A×C.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Torque τ = r × F with r = 2î + 3ĵ m, F = 4î − 5ĵ N: τ = |î ĵ k̂; 2 3 0; 4 −5 0| = k̂(−10 − 12) = −22k̂ N·m — 22 N·m clockwise (into the page).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A×B = 0 does NOT mean a zero vector — parallel vectors qualify too. Not associative: A×(B×C) ≠ (A×B)×C in general. No true cross product in 2D (only a scalar pseudo-product AxBy − AyBx).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Expand by components: A×B = (Axî+Ayĵ+Azk̂)×(Bxî+Byĵ+Bzk̂). Self-products vanish, anti-cyclic pairs flip sign, leaving (AyBz−AzBy)î + (AzBx−AxBz)ĵ + (AxBy−AyBx)k̂ — exactly the determinant, with |A×B| = AB sinθ following from |A|²|B|² − (A·B)² = A²B²sin²θ.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Memorise the cyclic order î→ĵ→k̂→î: forward = +, backward = −. Parallel → 0, perpendicular → max. |A×B| = parallelogram area, half of it = triangle area. Torque, magnetic force qv×B and angular momentum r×p are all the same product.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style (see the unit's NEB exam focus note): define the vector product and state the right-hand rule; distinguish dot vs cross product; compute A×B for given vectors and use it for torque/magnetic-force numericals.
